sections.h2: Who records a deed in Alcona County, and how do you reach the office?
sections.html:
The Alcona County Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages and other papers that affect land in the county. The county directory lists the office at 989-724-9450, with a fax line at 989-724-9459, and the county seat is Harrisville.

The office is part of the Alcona County Building, and its page on the county site says the duties come from state law. The staff do not draft documents or answer legal questions, so a seller who needs a deed written should go to an attorney or the title company handling the sale.

The page lists what the office records: warranty and quitclaim deeds, mortgages and their assignments and discharges, land contracts, liens and lien releases, easements, rights of way, oil and gas leases, plats, surveys, land corners and court orders that affect real property. It is also a U.S. passport acceptance facility, which explains why the counter can be busy.

The county posts a list of days the building is shut, and Columbus Day and Veterans Day appear on it along with Thanksgiving and the day after. Call before you drive to Harrisville with a signed deed, because a closed courthouse on a closing day can push a recording back.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Alcona County?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30.00 for each document, whatever its page count. That amount is set by MCL 600.2567, and the Alcona office page repeats it.

  • $30.00 to record a document, plus $3.00 for each added instrument when one paper assigns or discharges several.
  • $1.00 per page for a copy of a recorded record, and $5.00 more to certify it.
  • $5.00 for a tax certificate, which covers up to 5 property descriptions, with 20 cents for each extra description.
  • Mailed documents need a self-addressed stamped envelope, and an overpayment of $10.00 or less sent by mail is kept by the county.

Because of that last rule, count your check carefully when you send a deed through the mail. A seller who is unsure of the total can phone the office for the figure first.

sections.h2: Which Alcona County deeds need a tax certificate from the treasurer?
sections.html:
A warranty deed does, along with land contracts, assignments of land contracts, condominium master deeds, subdivision plats and any deed that conveys and warrants title. The register will not take those papers without a certificate from the Treasurer's Office, which you can reach at 989-724-9420.

Get the certificate before the deed is signed and attach it when the document goes to the register. The register's list names warranty-type deeds, so a seller using another kind of deed should ask which papers apply.

While you are at the treasurer's counter, ask whether any tax is still owed on the parcel. A buyer or title company will want any balance settled, so a seller does well to learn the figure early.

sections.h2: How much is the Michigan transfer tax on an Alcona County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays two taxes: $0.55 for each $500 of value under MCL 207.504 for the county, and $3.75 for each $500 under MCL 207.525 for the state. Any part of $500 counts as a full $500.

The Census Bureau lists a median value of $162,800 for owner-occupied homes in Alcona County for 2020 to 2024. A sale at that price crosses 326 units of $500, so the county tax is $179.30, the state tax is $1,222.50, and the two together come to $1,401.80.

The tax is owed to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed, under MCL 207.523. The deed must state the full value on its face, or an affidavit must be attached.

sections.h2: Which Alcona County transfers skip the transfer tax?
sections.html:
Several family and court transfers are exempt under MCL 207.526. Most sellers in a cash sale will not qualify, but heirs and relatives sometimes do.

  • A deed from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child.
  • A deed from a grandparent to a grandchild, step-grandchild or adopted grandchild.
  • A conveyance between spouses that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A transfer where the price is under $100.
  • A deed given to confirm title already held, such as one that fixes a flaw.

A seller who paid the tax and later believes an exemption applied can ask the state Department of Treasury for a refund, as the statute describes.

sections.h2: What makes the register reject a deed in Alcona County?
sections.html:
The register may refuse a paper that misses a format rule in MCL 565.201. Most failures are small layout problems that a title company catches in advance.

  • A blank margin of at least 2 1/2 inches at the top of page one and 1/2 inch on the other sides.
  • A first line that names the single recordable event the paper shows, such as a warranty deed.
  • Type of 10 points or larger, in black ink on white paper of at least 20 pound weight.
  • Sheets between 8 1/2 by 11 and 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • The name and business address of the person who drafted it.

A paper that lists more than one recordable event on its first line cannot be recorded, so do not combine a deed and a mortgage release on a single sheet.

sections.h2: What is Alcona County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Alcona County is the first county alphabetically in Michigan, and its flag says "First of 83." It was set up in 1840, organized in 1869, and covers 1,791 square miles, of which 62 percent is water. Lake Huron forms the eastern edge, Hubbard Lake is one of the state's twenty largest inland lakes, and the Au Sable River crosses the southwest.

Harrisville is the only city and the county seat. Lincoln is the village, and the townships named on the county site are Alcona, Caledonia, Curtis, Gustin, Greenbush, Harrisville, Haynes, Millen and Mitchell. Part of the Huron National Forest lies inside the county, and the Alcona Dam stands on the Au Sable in Curtis Township.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 10,556 residents spread over about 15 people per square mile. Some 37.4 percent are 65 or older, and 89.6 percent of homes are owner occupied. Median household income is $54,993, and the mean drive to work is 27.9 minutes, longer than in nearby Alpena County.

Building, zoning and assessment work sits with townships and the county Equalization Department at 989-724-9430. The Building Department is at 989-724-9440. A seller with a permit question or an assessment question should start with those offices before the deed is drafted.

faqs.q: How much does the Alcona County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: It charges $30.00 per document. An extra $3.00 applies for each additional instrument when a single paper assigns or discharges more than one, and copies are $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a house sells in Alcona County?
faqs.a: The seller is liable for it under MCL 207.523. The county share is $0.55 per $500 of value and the state share is $3.75 per $500, paid to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need the treasurer to sign off before I record a warranty deed in Alcona County?
faqs.a: Yes, a warranty deed needs a tax certificate from the Alcona County Treasurer's Office. The certificate costs $5.00 for up to five descriptions, and the Treasurer's phone line is 989-724-9420.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Alcona County register?
faqs.a: Yes, but include a self-addressed stamped envelope for its return. The office keeps any overpayment of $10.00 or less that arrives with a mailed document.

faqs.q: Can I search Alcona County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes, through two paid services the register's page names, Laredo, a subscription search, and Tapestry, another fee-based search. Ask the office about Laredo access by calling 989-724-9450.
